reviews.text: Ferrous had an excellent experience at your hospital - as usual!

I was incredibly worried when my pet cat, Rooster, wasn’t feeling well, and Dundas Euclid Animal Hospital was there for me. What meant the most to me was that they took the time to listen to my concerns, thoroughly assess Rooster, and explain everything clearly.

They gave me different options for his care without judgment or pressure, which made an incredibly stressful situation feel much more manageable. I never felt rushed or judged for the decisions I was making for my pet. Instead, I felt supported and respected throughout the entire process.

They treated Rooster with so much compassion and genuinely cared about his wellbeing. As a pet owner, knowing you have a veterinary team that will support both you and your animal means so much.

I’m incredibly grateful to the entire team at Dundas Euclid for taking such wonderful care of Rooster and for making a difficult experience a little easier.

———
In response to the comment below, my negative review is in regards to:
1.	The lack of professionalism from your staff when I was informed that I wouldn’t be able to keep my appointment. The staff member could have at least said, “I’m sorry, we’ve been trying to reach you but were unable to get a hold of you.” Instead, I was greeted with “We’ve called you four times and emailed you,” without even a simple “hello” or “good morning.”
2.	The contact information should have been verified when the appointment was confirmed, but this was not done. I was the one who called the receptionist to inform them that my dog needed anxiety medication before the appointment, and I also requested a refill. After not receiving a callback, I used the remaining medication from my last visit to your office, which is why I showed up for the appointment.
3.	Had I received the phone calls and “lengthy email” as mentioned, I would not have shown up for the appointment. Clearly, I did not receive them, and I take issue with the implication that I would have shown up regardless, especially knowing my dog has anxiety at the vet.

I will not be rescheduling, as it’s clear your front desk staff needs customer service training.

They are angels. I've put them through a lot in getting original paperwork mailed to me and through the Canada Post strike and all. And they are so good about it. I'm surprised because we are not a current client and they just were so willing to help!

I didn’t realize when healthcare was cut the vets followed.

Last check up, the vet didn’t give my dog her regular set of vaccines and I only noticed when I got home and looked at the invoice.
Vet said her teeth showed mild build up but when I went home I noticed one of her teeth was wobbly. This should have been discussed.

My dog also gets sick every time she leaves this vet and ends up with bloody diarrhea.
We get a checkup ($140) and get some vaccines ($) and poop test ($125), dog is fine and then in a few weeks bloody diarrhea, get another checkup ($140) and another poop test ($125) and go home with some antibiotics ($) and probiotics ($), and finally get the poop test results in a few days.

If you choose to go to this vet, make sure you manage their tasks like training a new employee. You are the one that pays for their mistakes and oversights and talking to their receptionists feel like you’re calling Walmart to address missing items from your order

Prescription power is the only reason why I keep going here

Update:
I asked if possible to dispense antibiotics without an exam since there was no space available for my pet to be seen.
